subject: ela
intro: When we read two different texts about the same topic, we can compare and contrast them. Comparing means finding what is the same. Contrasting means finding what is different. Each text may include some of the same important points and some different details. Good readers notice what both texts share and what makes each one unique.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Dolphins are smart ocean mammals. They live in groups called pods and communicate with clicks and whistles.'

Text B: 'Dolphins are highly intelligent animals that live in the ocean. They travel together in groups and use sounds to talk to each other.'

What do both texts have in common? What is one difference?

steps: I read Text A. It says dolphins are smart, live in pods, and communicate with clicks and whistles.
I read Text B. It says dolphins are highly intelligent, live in the ocean, travel in groups, and use sounds to communicate.
Both texts say dolphins are intelligent and live in groups in the ocean.
One difference: Text A uses the specific word 'pods' for the group and names the specific sounds (clicks and whistles). Text B just says 'groups' and 'sounds' without those details.
solution.answer: Both texts say that dolphins are intelligent and live in groups in the ocean and communicate with sounds. One difference is that Text A uses specific vocabulary like 'pods' and 'clicks and whistles,' while Text B uses more general language like 'groups' and 'sounds.'

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'The sun is a giant ball of hot gas. It is the center of our solar system. Earth takes 365 days to travel around the sun.'

Text B: 'The sun gives Earth light and warmth. Plants need sunlight to grow. Without the sun, there would be no life on Earth.'

What is one important point that both texts make about the sun? What is each text most focused on?

steps: I read Text A. It describes what the sun is (hot gas), where it is (center of the solar system), and Earth's orbit.
I read Text B. It describes what the sun does for Earth: provides light and warmth, helps plants grow, supports life.
Both texts agree that the sun is important. That is something they share.
Text A focuses on what the sun IS (its physical nature and position). Text B focuses on what the sun DOES (its effects on Earth and life).
solution.answer: Both texts agree that the sun is important to Earth. Text A focuses on what the sun is physically (a giant ball of hot gas at the center of our solar system). Text B focuses on what the sun does for life on Earth (provides light, warmth, and supports plant growth).

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Earthquakes happen when large sections of rock underground suddenly shift. They can shake buildings and cause damage. Scientists use instruments called seismographs to measure earthquakes.'

Text B: 'Earthquakes are dangerous natural events. People who live in earthquake zones should keep an emergency kit with water, food, and a flashlight. Practicing earthquake drills helps families stay safe.'

What is the most important point that ONLY Text A makes? What is the most important point that ONLY Text B makes?

steps: Text A explains what causes earthquakes and how they are measured.
Text B explains how people can prepare for earthquakes and stay safe.
Neither text shares these specific points with the other.
Text A's unique point: earthquakes happen when underground rock shifts, and scientists measure them with seismographs.
Text B's unique point: people in earthquake zones should prepare emergency kits and practice drills.
solution.answer: Text A's unique important point is that earthquakes happen when underground rock shifts suddenly, and scientists use seismographs to measure them. Text B's unique important point is that people in earthquake zones should keep emergency kits and practice drills to stay safe. Text A focuses on science while Text B focuses on safety preparation.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Rainforests are found near the equator. They receive more than 80 inches of rain per year. Rainforests are home to more than half of all plant and animal species on Earth.'

Text B: 'Rainforests are being destroyed at an alarming rate. Thousands of acres are cut down each year for farming and lumber. Scientists warn that losing rainforests could cause many species to go extinct.'

Which text gives more information about why rainforests matter? Use details to explain.

steps: Text A gives facts about where rainforests are, how much rain they get, and how many species live there.
Text B explains that rainforests are being destroyed and that this threatens species extinction.
Both texts touch on species, but Text B explains the consequence of losing rainforests more deeply.
Text A gives background facts about what rainforests are. Text B explains why protecting them is urgent.
solution.answer: Text B gives more information about why rainforests matter by explaining what will happen if they are destroyed (species extinction). Text A gives useful background facts, but Text B makes the importance feel urgent by showing the danger. Together, Text A explains what rainforests are and Text B explains why we should care about them.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries. Millions of workers built it using stone, brick, and earth. The wall stretches thousands of miles across northern China.'

Text B: 'The Great Wall of China was built to protect China from invasions from the north. Soldiers were stationed along the wall to watch for enemies. Today, the wall is one of the most famous landmarks in the world.'

Identify one similarity and one difference between the two texts. Then explain which text gives more information about the wall's purpose.

steps: Similarity: Both texts are about the Great Wall of China.
Difference: Text A focuses on how the wall was built (materials, workers, length). Text B focuses on why it was built (protection from invasion) and its current status.
Purpose means reason for building. Text B directly says the wall was built to protect China from invasions.
Text A does not mention why the wall was built at all.
solution.answer: Similarity: Both texts are about the Great Wall of China and describe it as a large structure. Difference: Text A describes how the wall was built (materials and workers) while Text B explains why it was built (protection from invasion). Text B gives more information about the wall's purpose because it directly states the wall was meant to stop invasions from the north.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Honeybees live in colonies with a queen bee, worker bees, and drones. The queen lays eggs while worker bees gather food and make honey.'

Text B: 'Honeybees are important pollinators. As they fly from flower to flower collecting nectar, they spread pollen. This helps plants produce fruit and seeds.'

What is one thing both texts tell you about bees? What is each text mostly about?
items.hint: First, find what both texts mention. Then ask: what is the main idea of Text A? What is the main idea of Text B?

steps: Both texts mention bees and their activities.
Both show bees doing important work (making honey / pollinating plants).
Text A is mostly about how bees are organized in a colony.
Text B is mostly about how bees help plants through pollination.
solution.answer: Both texts tell you that bees do important work. Text A is mostly about how a bee colony is organized, with a queen, workers, and drones. Text B is mostly about how bees help plants by spreading pollen when they collect nectar.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Penguins live in cold regions like Antarctica. They huddle together in large groups to stay warm in freezing temperatures.'

Text B: 'Penguins are excellent swimmers. They use their flipper-like wings to zoom through the water at high speeds to catch fish.'

Identify one similarity and one difference in what the two texts say about penguins.
items.hint: For the similarity, think about what both texts tell you about how penguins survive. For the difference, think about what activity each text focuses on.

steps: Similarity: Both texts describe how penguins survive in their environment. Text A shows they stay warm by huddling. Text B shows they catch food by swimming.
Difference: Text A is about how penguins handle cold weather. Text B is about how penguins swim and hunt for food.
solution.answer: Similarity: Both texts describe survival strategies that penguins use. Difference: Text A focuses on how penguins survive cold temperatures by huddling together, while Text B focuses on how penguins swim and catch fish.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Rosa Parks was a civil rights leader. In 1955, she refused to give up her seat on a bus to a white passenger. Her action helped spark a famous bus boycott in Montgomery, Alabama.'

Text B: 'Rosa Parks worked for equal rights for many years. She helped organize peaceful protests and worked with civil rights groups. She received many awards for her brave work.'

Which text gives more information about a single important event? Which text gives more information about Rosa Parks's long career?
items.hint: Think about whether each text talks about one specific moment or about Rosa Parks's life over a longer period of time.

steps: Text A describes one specific event in 1955 and its result.
Text B describes her long career of organizing protests and receiving awards.
Text A gives more information about a single important event.
Text B gives more information about her long career.
solution.answer: Text A gives more information about a single important event: her refusal to give up her bus seat in 1955 and the boycott it sparked. Text B gives more information about her long career by describing her work organizing protests and the awards she received over many years.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'Tornadoes are spinning columns of wind. They form from powerful thunderstorms. The fastest tornadoes can have winds over 300 miles per hour.'

Text B: 'Tornadoes are very dangerous. If a tornado warning is issued, go to the lowest floor of a building and stay away from windows. A basement or interior room is the safest place to be.'

Identify one similarity and two differences between the two texts. Then explain which text would be more useful to someone who just heard a tornado warning.
items.hint: For the similarity, think about what both texts are discussing. For the differences, think about whether each text is about science facts or safety steps.

steps: Similarity: Both texts are about tornadoes.
Difference 1: Text A gives science facts about what tornadoes are and how fast they are. Text B gives safety instructions.
Difference 2: Text A says tornadoes form from thunderstorms. Text B says to go to the lowest floor and avoid windows.
For someone who just heard a warning, Text B is more useful because it tells them what to do right now.
solution.answer: Similarity: Both texts are about tornadoes. Differences: Text A gives science facts about what tornadoes are and how fast they move. Text B gives safety steps to follow during a tornado warning. Text B would be more useful to someone who just heard a warning because it tells them exactly what to do to stay safe, while Text A gives background information but no safety advice.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Text A: 'The Amazon River in South America is one of the longest rivers in the world. It carries more water than any other river. Thousands of species of fish live in it.'

Text B: 'The Amazon River is in danger. Pollution from farms and cities flows into the river. Overfishing has reduced the number of fish in some areas.'

Which text gives more information about the Amazon River? Use at least two details from each text to explain your answer.
items.hint: Think about what each text adds to your understanding of the Amazon River. Together, do the two texts give you a more complete picture than either one alone?

steps: Text A gives facts about the river's size, water volume, and fish species.
Text B gives information about threats the river faces: pollution and overfishing.
Neither text gives more information overall; they each give different types of information.
Together they give a fuller picture: what the river is and what is threatening it.
solution.answer: Neither text alone gives more information overall; they cover different aspects. Text A tells us the river is very long, carries the most water of any river, and has thousands of fish species. Text B tells us pollution from farms and cities is harming the river and overfishing has reduced fish numbers. Together, the two texts give a fuller picture: Text A shows why the river is remarkable and Text B shows why it needs to be protected.
